correctness.rationale: Colored pair-of-matchings decomposition is bijective and exhaustive, including double edges. Each path rank equals its smaller vertex class, and each cycle rank is k except exactly when char two or k even, by determinant 1-(-1)^k and one-dimensional kernel. Labeled path/cycle exponential weights give the full coefficient identity. Nonsingular pairs use only balanced paths and nonsingular cycles; a local Gaussian saddle expansion with controlled tails gives exact leading constants. Exhaustive independent elimination agrees for all pairs through n=4 over characteristic 2 and 3; formal total consistency is checked through n=8. These checks do not replace the symbolic proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Existing full-permutation matrix classifications restrict to a proper subset of rook-matrix pairs and therefore cannot imply aggregate counts over all partially defined maps; ordinary random finite-field matrix rank results sample a different ensemble with no matching constraint. The general rook-monoid order formula alone does not determine the rank of an additive sum.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The sum rank is equivalent to the rank of a degree-two bicolored bipartite matching adjacency block with row and column vertices, or equivalently to its colored path-cycle decomposition. The full permutation pair special case admits only cycles and is prior coverage. The partial pair model also admits paths; these produce nonsingular sums in characteristic two and an additional exponential component absent in full permutation work. No located source supplied the resulting joint rook-monoid rank polynomial or its asymptotic probability.

value.rationale: Additive ranks in the natural matrix embedding of the inverse semigroup form a motivated structural invariant distinct from multiplicative rank. The exact polynomial solves every finite-size rank stratum. Its full-rank specialization exhibits a sharp characteristic-dependent polynomial prefactor and common stretched-exponential exponent for a natural growing random ensemble, revealing a robust structural cancellation rather than a small special case.
